mechanism: Mycophenolate can cause diarrhea and GI dysmotility, impairing potassium absorption, while concurrent potassium supplementation increases hyperkalemia risk, particularly in patients with renal impairment or concurrent ACE inhibitors/ARBs.
action: Monitor serum potassium levels regularly; assess renal function; consider dietary potassium restriction or alternative immunosuppression if hyperkalemia develops; coordinate with other medications affecting potassium homeostasis.
